minutes.headline: DPW fuel tank cut failed; capital plan debate continued, with a motion to remove a rescue vehicle pending
minutes.summary: The 2019 annual Town Meeting opened, honored a retiring selectman, appointed a deputy moderator, and passed Articles 2 through 5 by voice vote. Most of the time went to Article 6, the capital plan, chiefly the DPW fuel tank replacement cost and the master plan money. An amendment to cut the fuel tank line failed, a motion to pass over the article failed, and the captions end during debate on a motion to remove the rescue vehicle.

public_comment.topic: Asked which capital requests were left out and why vertex report items were not funded; asked about voting machines and ranked choice.
Asked whether the old fire truck and ambulance would be traded or disposed of.
Proposed an amendment cutting the DPW fuel tank line by $100,000, citing uncertain estimates and school underfunding.
Said the only written professional quote for the tank work was higher than the town's figure.
Supported on-site tanks but questioned the amount and why the fire truck was not borrowed for.
Opposed the reduction; said tank location move addresses environmental concern.
Suggested deferring other capital items to fund schools and operations.
Concerned no building maintenance is in the plan; suggested passing over the article until articles 21-24 are decided.
Prefers paying cash for capital over debt given weak debt rating.
Questioned the fifty thousand dollars for another master plan.
Moved to remove the master plan money, saying there were no written details.

what_happened.line: An amendment to cut the DPW fuel tank line in the capital plan failed, after a motion to end debate on it passed.
A motion to pass over the capital plan article failed, so debate on the plan continued.
The capital plan article, funding fourteen projects with no borrowing, was presented; the vote on it was not audible in the captions.
Articles 2 through 5, covering revolving funds, prior year expenses and fiscal 19 budget transfers, passed unanimously.
The captions end during debate on a motion to remove the rescue vehicle; the master plan amendment result was not audible.

why_it_matters: The capital plan sets what the town pays for in cash from taxes and free cash rather than by borrowing, so each line kept or cut affects the tax bill and what is left for schools and building upkeep.
The fuel tank project is expected to draw on a state earmark that is specific to that project, with unspent money returning to town funds, so the net local cost depends on that earmark.
watch_next: The final vote on Article 6, the capital plan, and the outcomes of the master plan and rescue vehicle amendments, none of which are clear in these captions.
